object_description: lightweight upper volume on a solid base with a modulated roofscape
design_condition: Offset westward from the existing building, the volume enlarges the entrance area, maintains distance from the outdoor pools, and forms shaded, sunken, and embanked outdoor spaces around the bathing complex.

positive.statement: The new building integrates into the existing situation and connects seamlessly to the existing site.
The modulated roof landscape and facade design with its choice of materials and fenestration are impressive.
The operational processes are well resolved and the bathroom floor is spatially structured in an appealing way.
The arrangement of the pools is ideal from the user's perspective.
The covered intermediate zone supports the desired indoor-outdoor connection.
The relatively small area and volume promise comparatively low construction costs, and the wooden construction is a first step toward sustainability.

negative.statement: The measures intended to upgrade the traffic area into a square could be stronger and more effective spatially.
The interior atmosphere appears dematerialized and still needs to be detailed as work continues.
The route through the cloakrooms and the ability to find the stairs to the upper floor must be made clearer.
The entrance to the cafeteria outside swimming times is hardly recognizable as public access.
The non-swimmer and multipurpose pool area must be increased, and a direct workshop-to-technical-room connection is desired.
